newsitem.title: UK: ICI shares drop after Q1 profit tumble.
newsitem.headline: ICI shares drop after Q1 profit tumble.

text.p: Shares in Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc dropped in early trading on Thursday after the company announced a sharp fall in profits in the first quarter of the year.
The stock was down 15-1/2p at 705 by 0708.

Profit expectations for the group have already been lowered in recent months, one reason the stock dropped ten percent in the first three months of the year, but the latest figure still appears worse than analysts had expected.
Pre-tax profits before exceptional items dropped to 65 million stg from 202 million a year before, compared with expectations mostly in a range between 75 million stg and 90 million.
Dealers noted that ICI was suffering a price squeeze in chemicals such as polyester and tioxide and said the figures could be the cue for further downgrades to earnings expectations.
"They are having big problems in industrial chemicals and there is still intense price competiton," said one, "what they have done to control costs hasn't really worked."

However, he noted that the outlook for the second half was better and said that the stock should benefit when sterling's recent surge runs out of steam -- easing the pressure on export earnings that ICI and other international companies have suffered.
Some 40 million stg of ICI's profit decline in the first quarter was due to sterling strength, ICI said.
"As soon as sterling turns round you won't see this stock for dust," the dealer said.
